description: GeoGuard Kerala is a free web app that helps Kerala families understand and prepare for flood and storm risk. It uses NASA POWER to show 20+ years of rainfall trends (monsoon patterns, heavy-rain days, wet streaks), NASA EONET to show open natural hazard events, and NASA GIBS satellite imagery to show current conditions. An action layer turns the data into simple before, during and after checklists for floods, landslides and cyclones. Built solo for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.
summary: GeoGuard Kerala is a free web app that helps Kerala families understand and prepare for flood and storm risk. For any of Kerala’s 14 districts, it uses 25 years of NASA POWER rainfall data to show the wettest months, heavy-rain days per year, the longest wet streaks and how this year compares with normal, so people can see long-term trends in their own area. A Now tab maps open natural hazard events from NASA EONET over NASA GIBS satellite imagery and ranks them by distance. An Act tab turns the data into before, during and after checklists for floods, landslides and cyclones, in English and Malayalam, printable for families. It addresses the Earth System Trend Detective challenge by making NASA Earth data usable for local decisions.
details:
What it does: GeoGuard Kerala has three tabs. Risk: for each Kerala district, it analyses daily rainfall from NASA POWER (2001 to now) to show average monthly rainfall against this year, heavy-rain days per year, the longest wet streak per year, and a relative flood-prone-season indicator. Now: an interactive map shows open hazard events from NASA EONET, ranked by distance from the chosen district, over NASA GIBS satellite imagery with a date picker. Act: before, during and after checklists for floods, landslides, cyclones and emergency basics, saved in the browser, printable, and available in English and Malayalam.

Impact: Kerala families get alerts but rarely see their own long-term pattern or know what to do. GeoGuard turns open NASA Earth data into plain-language trends and actions.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Leaflet (maps) and Chart.js (charts). No backend.

Creativity: it combines long-term trend analysis (POWER) with current events and imagery (EONET, GIBS) and an action layer in the local language.

Limits we state openly: POWER data is historical, not a forecast, and is gridded (about 50 km), so it smooths local extremes. EONET lists only significant events. The risk levels are relative indicators, not warnings. It does not replace IMD or KSDMA alerts. The Malayalam text has not been reviewed by a native speaker.

AI use: the code and checklist text were written with help from an AI assistant (Claude by Anthropic) and tested by the team owner.
